entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Heard Mr. Mohammad Waseem, the learned counsel for applicant- Smt. Ishrat, Mr. Rajeev Kumar
Singh Parmar, the learned counsel for applicant- Talib and the learned A.G.A. for State.
Perused the record.

This application for bail has been filed by applicants- Smt Ishrat and Talib seeking their enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 356 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station- Bithari Chainpur, District- Bareilly, during the pendency of trial.
Record shows that marriage of Talib, son of applicant Smt. Ishrat was solemnized with Rajvee on 30.6.2019 in accordance with Muslim Rites and Customs.

However, even before expiry of a period of three years from the date of marriage of the son of applicant, Smt. Ishrat an unfortunate incident occurred on 14.6.2022, in which daughter-in-law of applicant Smt. Ishrat sustained burn injuries.
It is the case of applicant that victim was rushed to hospital by husband of the deceased i.e. applicant Talib.
Unfortunately, the injured died as she scummed to the injuries sustained by her while undergoing treatment.
The information regarding the death of deceased at the concerned police station was given by ward-boy of concerned hospital.
On the aforesaid information, the inquest (panchayatnama) of the deceased was conducted.
In the opinion of witnesses of inquest (panch witnesses) the nature of death of deceased was characterized as homicidal.
Thereafter post mortem of the body of deceased was conducted.

The autopsy surgeon who conducted autopsy of the body of deceased found following antemortem injuries on the body of deceased:
"superficial to deep burn injury present over the over face, both side of chest, whole both side of book.
Both rod bedlocck, aral both hands sirging of hair line of red."
In the opinion of autopsy surgeon, the cause of death of deceased was shock due to ante-mortem extensive burn injuries.

After aforementioned proceedings were completed, first informant-Saleem (father of the deceased)
lodged a delayed F.I.R. dated 15.6.2022, which was registered as Case Crime No. 356 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station- Bithari Chainpur, District- Bareilly.

In the aforesaid F.I.R., five persons namely, Talib (father-in-law), Ishrat (mother-in-law),
Najreen, Sanobar (sister-in-law) and Guddu (Nandoi) have been nominated as named accused.
After aforesaid F.I.R. was lodged Investigating Officer proceeded with statutory investigation of concerned case crime number in terms of Chapter XII Cr.P.C.

During course of investigation,
Investigating Officer examined first informant and other witnesses under section 161 Cr.P.C.
Witnesses so examined have supported the F.I.R.
On the basis of above and other material collected by Investigating Officer during course of investigation, he came to the conclusion that complicity of Talib is established in the crime in question.
Accordingly he submitted the charge sheet dated 13.9.2022 against applicant Talib.
This was followed by the supplementary charge-sheet dated 20.7.2023, whereby Ishrat has been charge sheeted.
The investigation in respect of other co-accused is said to be pending.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicants contend that even though the applicants are named as well as charge sheeted accused, yet they are liable to be enlarged on bail.

Referring to the provisions contained in proviso to section 437 Cr.P.C., learned counsel for applicant contends that since applicant Ishrat is the mother-in-law of deceased, therefore she is liable to be enlarged on bail.
It is then contended that applicant is a woman of clean antecedents, having no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
The police report in terms of Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. i.e. charge sheet has already been submitted.
As such, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by prosecution against applicants stands crystalized.
However, up to this stage, no such incriminating circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the course of trial.
He further contends that applicant Ishrat cannot be said to be the beneficiary of alleged demand of dowry.

Even otherwise,
allegations made in F.I.R., i.e. demand of additional dowry and bullet motorcycle are vague allegations, as the same are devoid of material particulars.
The same has not been detailed in the statement of the first informant either.
Resultantly, the same is liable to be ignored by this court at this stage.
Applicant Ishrat is in jail since 25.4.2023.
As such, she has undergone more than three months of incarceration.
It is thus urged that applicant Smt Ishrat is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case applicant Ishrat is enlarged on bail she shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
Mr. Rajeev Kumar Singh Parmar, the learned counsel for applicant- Talib submits that applicant is husband of the deceased.
Irrespective of above, he is liable to be enlarged on bail.
The bonafide of applicant is explicit from the fact that after the occurrence had taken place, applicant Talib had taken the victim to the hospital.
He has also adopted the arguments urged by learned counsel for applicant- Smt Ishrat.
He, therefore, contends that applicant- Talib is also liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has opposed the present applications for bail.
He submits that the death of the deceased is an unnatural death.
The occurrence leading to the death of the deceased has occurred in the marital home of the deceased and within three years of marriage.
Thus the death of deceased is a dowry death.
As such, burden is upon the applicant to explain the manner of occurrence and also his innocence.
However, up to this stage, applicants have failed to discharge their burden regarding above as per Sections 106 and 113 B of the Evidence act Act.
On the above premise, learned A.G.A. submits that no sympathy be shown by this Court in favour of applicants.

Having heard the learned counsel for applicants, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of material brought on record, evidence, nature and gravity of offence as well as the complicity of applicants and accusation made coupled with the fact that Smt. Ishrat is mother-in-law of the deceased, therefore by virtue of the provisions contained in proviso to Section 437 Cr.P.C. she is liable to be enlarged on bail, the clean antecedents, the period of incarceration undergone, and also the fact that the police report in terms of Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. i.e. charge sheet has already been submitted, but without making any comment on the merits of the case, applicant- Smt Ishrat has made out a case for bail.
Accordingly, the bail application of Applicant- Smt Ishrat is Allowed.

sentences.text:
Let the applicant - Smt Ishrat, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) THE APPLICANT SHALL FILE AN UNDERTAKING TO THE EFFECT THAT HE/SHE SHALL NOT SEEK ANY ADJOURNMENT ON THE DATE FIXED FOR EVIDENCE WHEN THE WITNESSES ARE PRESENT IN COURT.
IN CASE OF DEFAULT OF THIS CONDITION, IT SHALL BE OPEN FOR THE TRIAL COURT TO TREAT IT AS ABUSE OF LIBERTY OF BAIL AND PASS ORDERS IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.
(ii) THE APPLICANT SHALL REMAIN PRESENT BEFORE THE TRIAL COURT ON EACH DATE FIXED, EITHER PERSONALLY OR THROUGH HIS/HER COUNSEL.
IN CASE OF HIS/HER ABSENCE, WITHOUT SUFFICIENT CAUSE, THE TRIAL COURT MAY PROCEED AGAINST HIM/HER UNDER SECTION 229-A IPC.

(iii) IN CASE, THE APPLICANT MISUSES THE LIBERTY OF BAIL DURING TRIAL AND IN ORDER TO SECURE HIS/HER PRESENCE PROCLAMATION UNDER SECTION 82 CR.P.C., MAY BE ISSUED AND IF APPLICANT FAILS TO APPEAR BEFORE THE COURT ON THE DATE FIXED IN SUCH PROCLAMATION, THEN,
THE TRIAL COURT SHALL INITIATE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST HIM/HER, IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW, UNDER SECTION 174-A IPC.
(iv) THE APPLICANT SHALL REMAIN PRESENT, IN PERSON, BEFORE THE TRIAL COURT ON DATES FIXED FOR (1) OPENING OF THE CASE, (2) FRAMING OF CHARGE AND (3) RECORDING OF STATEMENT UNDER SECTION 313 CR.P.C.

IF IN THE OPINION OF THE TRIAL COURT ABSENCE OF THE APPLICANT IS DELIBERATE OR WITHOUT SUFFICIENT CAUSE, THEN IT SHALL BE OPEN FOR THE TRIAL COURT TO TREAT SUCH DEFAULT AS ABUSE OF LIBERTY OF BAIL AND PROCEED AGAINST THE HIM/HER IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.
(v) THE TRIAL COURT MAY MAKE ALL POSSIBLE EFFORTS/ENDEAVOUR AND TRY TO CONCLUDE THE TRIAL WITHIN A PERIOD OF ONE YEAR AFTER THE RELEASE OF THE APPLICANT.

However, it is made clear that any wilful violation of above conditions by the applicant, shall have serious repercussion on his/her bail so granted by this court and the trial court is at liberty to cancel the bail, after recording the reasons for doing so, in the given case of any of the condition mentioned above.
However, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, as noted herein above, this Court does not find any good ground to enlarge the applicant-Talib on bail.

Accordingly bail application of applicant-Talib is liable to be rejected.
The bail application of Applicant-Talib is rejected.
